transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-07
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Planned duration: 75 minutes
Actual attendees: see metadata list above

Summary:
Leadership gave a short state-of-the-company, covered hiring posture, runway, product priorities for Q1 and Q2, and opened an extended Q&A/open-mic for team questions. There was a frank conversation about costs, dedicated vs hosted product motion, and career path clarity.

Topics:
- Business health and runway
- Hiring & leveling / career ladders
- Product priorities: Console, Optimize, Private deploys
- Cost/perf levers and infra playbook
- Security posture and compliance cadence
- Open-mic Q&A (people ops, manager expectations, remote policy)

Action items (recap at end): see metadata.action_items

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sabrina Li: Alright folks, good morning, thanks for joining. We'll run a bit long today, about an hour and a quarter, status update then open mic for questions. Marcus, quick infra needle?

[00:28] Marcus Ochoa: Yeah, short. We closed the quarter slightly ahead of plan on hosted revenue, cost is still the story though. Our unit economics improved with the batching changes but there's more to do — e.g., cross-tenant KV cache hit rates could be better, and we found some edge tail latency in certain region routing.

[00:52] Liam Chen: To add, the Dedicated fleet utilization is at 78% so burst capacity is burning cash. We're looking at smarter packing and preemptible windows for non-critical workloads. There's a trade we want to be explicit about: latency SLOs vs cost-savings.

[01:15] Sabrina Li: Important to say here we're not in a panic but we are tightening. Hiring will be selective, we will keep forward motion on key hires. Rosa? People update?

[01:34] Rosa Martinez: Quick people note — we reopened some IC ladders for review. Expect a clearer leveling doc this week. We're also piloting a career conversation toolkit for managers, because folks asked for more clarity in the pulse and last skip-levels.

[01:55] Audience: (murmurs)

[02:05] Priya Nambiar: On product: Q1 is about Console polish, better dashboards for route-level latency and token cost, plus Optimize v2 which includes quantization suggestions and auto-batching profiles. Private deployments get a focused sprint for cert automation and KMS/HSM integrations.

[02:36] Nora Feldman (from attendees): Will that include RBAC work? We have specific customers pushing for fine-grained access at route level.

[02:46] Priya Nambiar: Yup — RBAC is in the scope for Console Q1. Also audit logs are getting a retention tiering option.

[03:05] Speaker 6 (Ethan, SRE): Quick ops question — are we changing our default eviction for KV caches? Some POCs saw cache churn with longer sequences and it didn't align with our heuristics.

[03:22] Marcus Ochoa: We're tuning eviction thresholds and adding some telemetry to detect when prefixes get evicted too early. Also exploring per-customer cache quotas in Dedicated to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

[03:45] Sabrina Li: Thanks. Now open mic — please keep questions concise so we can get to as many as possible.

[04:00] [Time jump — many questions in open mic, snippets below]

[04:02] Julian Park: Curious about runway math — can you explain the assumptions behind the 'tighten hiring' message?

[04:18] Sabrina Li: Yes. We looked at three scenarios; the conservative one assumes slower upsell and longer sales cycles in mid-market while we continue to invest in product-led growth. We need a modest reduction in burn by optimizing infra and pacing hires. We think we can do this without pausing core projects.

[04:45] Julian Park: Ok thanks — helpful.

[05:00] Maya Singh (CS): Are there changes to the customer onboarding SLA? Customers keep asking for stricter latency guarantees for dedicated.

[05:12] Liam Chen: SLA language won't change immediately but we're offering Dedicated customers a higher SLA tier with additional cost. We also will document best practices for customers to hit latency targets with specific model variants and quantization profiles.

[05:34] [05:34] Samir Patel (Security): A quick security note — SOC2 Type 2 audit starts Feb 8. We're drafting boundary docs now. If teams are doing changes to logging, please flag us, we need to keep the audit trail intact.

[05:52] Sabrina Li: Great point Samir. Also, for Private deployments we are standardizing an installer that includes alignment with KMS and HSM workflows to make attestation easier.

[06:10] Unknown voice: Will that help customers who need on-prem air gap?

[06:16] Marcus Ochoa: Yes, part of the Private sprint is an air-gap installer package and docs; it's a heavy lift but a big revenue enabler for regulated customers.

[06:30] [06:30] Someone: Follow-up on career ladders — what about leveling for senior engineers that are IC-first?

[06:45] Rosa Martinez: We're adding dual-track examples — manager and IC. Each role will have clear expectations and examples of scope/impact. We'll publish by Friday and we'll run Q&A sessions for teams.

[07:05] Sabrina Li: Ok, two more rapid-fire topics: remote vs office posture and performance reviews.

[07:12] Rosa Martinez: We aren't mandating a return; teams should set norms. We'll be clearer on expectations for synchronous work and meeting etiquette. Performance reviews will be calibrated with the new ladders.

[07:33] Speaker: (someone asks about promotion timing)

[07:40] Rosa Martinez: Promotions will happen on a quarterly cadence; manager calibration meetings are scheduled after the ladder doc goes live.

[07:55] [Q&A continues, some cross-talk and filler]

[08:05] Priya Nambiar: On product roadmaps — customers keep asking for tooling around model audits and explainability; we're scoping a lightweight evals dashboard to show prompt sets, passthrough failure modes, and quality regressions. This is not full-scale research, it's operational tooling for teams.

[08:34] Nora Feldman: Will evals tie into Optimize?

[08:39] Priya Nambiar: Yes, eventually. The plan is to surface regressions when we roll model variants and to tie quality alerts to our rollout policies.

[09:01] Evan (Engine): Are there any changes to the on-call rota as we try to reduce burn?

[09:07] Liam Chen: We'll pilot a two-week rotation with shadowing to reduce cognitive load. Also moving some alerts to lower-noise channels and leveraging more of our observability retention to do better triage before paging.

[09:24] Sabrina Li: We're also running a retrospective on the last incident — will share the doc and learnings next week.

[09:36] [Half-hour mark summary — many small items discussed]

[30:05] Open mic continued: variety of questions around equity refreshers, mentee programs, pairing rotations. Leadership answers indicate more formalization coming.

[36:12] External reference (Sabrina): We're watching competitor pricing moves — Anthropic and OpenAI have introduced cheaper tokens at short context lengths, so our Optimize recommendations may shift to favor shorter contexts and higher batching when quality allows.

[37:00] Marcus Ochoa: Technically, we can adjust kernel selection heuristics to favor faster attention paths when sequence length is small. There's a bit of risk with hallucination profiles for some models, so product will own the guardrails.

[37:46] Q from product: Are we comfortable pushing default quantized profiles to hosted?

[37:53] Priya Nambiar: Not wide default yet; we'll use rollout policies and quality evals to push to cohorts. We'll share benchmarks with the org.

[38:30] [Longer discussion on canaries and rollback tooling — some audio overlap, speech fragments]

[40:12] Sabrina Li: Quick finance note — we're renegotiating some cloud contracts and expecting modest rate reductions in Q2. That said, we still need to reduce Dedicated footprint against utilization targets.

[41:00] Actionable question: How do we measure success for the cost program?

[41:08] Liam Chen: We'll track cost per 1k generated tokens, tail latency at p95 and p99, and Dedicated utilization. Targets and dashboards will be published in the infra playbook.

[41:30] Sabrina Li: Okay we're nearing the last 20 minutes — a few community questions from Slack were pulled in.

[42:05] Question (anonymous): Will there be more public-facing benchmarks for our model catalog? People want to point prospects to consistent numbers.

[42:22] Priya Nambiar: Yes — we'll publish an updated model catalog with curated benchmarks and recommended use cases. We'll also include a small 'cookbook' for common workloads.

[42:45] Another question: Can engineers get more time to contribute to open-source performance libs?

[42:54] Sabrina Li: We value the OSS work; we'll create a program for time credited monthly for maintainers and major contributors. We'll finalize details with managers.

[43:10] [43:10] People ops follow-ups: more manager training, a small stipend for home office refreshes, and mentorship pairing pilot.

[44:00] Rapid-fire Qs:
[44:02] Staff: "Can we get clarity on travel budget?"
[44:05] Rosa Martinez: Caps are unchanged, but approvals will be quicker for customer-facing trips.

[44:20] Staff: "Is there a plan for compensation market adjustments?"
[44:23] Rosa Martinez: We plan a targeted refresh for roles below staff engineer and ICs in high-demand tracks this quarter. Details in the HR doc.

[44:40] Staff: "Will we freeze hiring for interns/grad roles?"
[44:43] Sabrina Li: Intern hiring continues; graduating class hires will be considered case-by-case.

[45:00] [Mid-meeting stretch — some informal banter]

[46:30] Technical deep-dive snippet: Marcus describes kernel selection and sequence-length microbenchmarks; some folks ask about CUDA build matrix and quant libs. Transcription here is fuzzy — names like cuDNN and cust ? sometimes garbled.

[47:05] Marcus Ochoa: We'll open a short tech brown bag to dig into the CUDA/quant stack. Expect an invite.

[47:20] [People applause emojis mentioned in chat]

[48:00] Sabrina Li: Wrapping up — my ask to everyone is to lean into clarity: managers align with their teams on the priorities list, engineers think in terms of failure modes we can avoid, product own customer signals and what to deprioritize.

[48:24] Final Q&A snippets — some repeat.

[55:00] Closing recap by Sabrina: published docs this week (leveling + product priorities), infra will share playbook, people will run pulse, leadership will do a follow-up AMA.

[55:25] Sabrina Li: Thanks all. We'll follow up with a short notes doc and recording.

[55:33] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript fidelity: occasional mis-typed terms (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache") and truncated names are present; timestamps approximate only.
